note: Peer reviewed survey linking architecture choices to downstream limitations across biomedicine, vision language and code.
title: Large language models (LLMs): survey, technical frameworks, and future challenges

reading.body:
Architecture choices in large language models create predictable capability boundaries across biomedicine, vision, language, and code tasks, and these boundaries reflect fundamental tradeoffs rather than simple scaling problems.

The survey maps how design decisions propagate downstream into task performance. Models optimized for one capability often sacrifice another. These tradeoffs matter for compute allocation because throwing additional resources at a poorly-matched architecture yields diminishing returns. Understanding which architectural constraints are binding for a given application is prerequisite to knowing whether the solution is more compute, a different building approach, or something else entirely.

The paper does not isolate the power or infrastructure cost of different architectural choices, nor does it quantify the compute required to overcome specific limitations. It documents what works and what does not across domains, but not the resource economics of bridging those gaps. For organizations planning AI deployment, this means the survey identifies which capability boundaries exist, but leaves open the question of what resources crossing them demands.

explain_beginner: This paper surveys large language models, which are advanced AI systems that understand and generate human language. The research reviews how these models work, examines their use across different fields like medicine, image understanding, and software coding, and explores what they do well and where they fall short. The findings help readers understand current AI capabilities and suggest areas needing improvement for future progress.
explain_business: This survey identifies where large language models currently succeed and fail across practical applications including medical analysis, visual understanding, and software development. It reveals that while these systems show promise, fundamental limitations exist requiring new approaches. Organizations should understand these capability boundaries when planning AI deployment and recognize that continued investment in novel methodologies is necessary for meaningful advances beyond current model performance.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive survey examines large language model architectures and their implementation across multiple domains. The authors analyze foundational concepts including embeddings and deep learning techniques, review major model variants such as GPT-4 and PaLM, and document their applications in text generation, multimodal tasks, biomedicine, and code synthesis. The work systematically catalogs architectural design choices, identifies performance limitations across different tasks, and proposes new research directions for overcoming current constraints.
